sugestoes.texto: `tagDeviceUI` writes the device key to `localCache` before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice`. After the first `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, every request from the same device ID for the next 29 minutes returns nil from the cache, and `Authenticate` lets it through. Fix this by removing the cache entry on failure, or by caching only after the store call succeeds.

`pkg/server/wire.go:374-375` still registers `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and binds it to `AnonStore`. No provider supplies the new `int64` parameter, so wire code generation fails. It would fail anyway as an unused provider, because `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` now builds the store itself. Remove the provider and its bind from the wire set.

The device ID comes from a client-supplied header. An unauthenticated attacker can send `device_limit` requests with random IDs to fill every slot, and `Authenticate` then rejects all real anonymous users for up to 30 days. Add per-IP throttling for new device registrations, or degrade more gently (for example, keep authenticating but stop counting once the limit is reached).

By default, MySQL returns 0 affected rows when the UPDATE leaves the values unchanged. `updated_at` only has second precision, so a repeat update in the same second with the same IP and user agent returns 0. A device that is already registered then gets `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and fails authentication, for example when another instance doesn't share the local cache. Fix this by checking whether the row exists (SELECT within the window) instead of relying on `RowsAffected`.

Device tagging used to run in a background goroutine. It now runs synchronously on every anonymous request that misses the cache, and with a limit set it adds a `COUNT(*)` range scan over `anon_device` before the upsert, which adds DB latency to unauthenticated requests. Keep only the limit check on the request path and keep the upsert asynchronous, or cache the count.

`CountDevices` and the later insert/upsert run in separate DB sessions with no lock or transaction. Concurrent anonymous requests with new device IDs can all see `count < deviceLimit` and all insert, which pushes the number of active devices past the configured `device_limit`. Do the count and the insert inside one transaction with appropriate locking, or use a conditional INSERT ... SELECT that checks the count in the same statement.

issues.descricao: The device limit check counts devices and then inserts in separate non-atomic steps, so concurrent requests from new devices can all pass the check and exceed the configured limit.
issues.textoGolden: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

comentarios.texto: The limit check counts devices and then inserts in separate steps with no lock or transaction. Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit is exceeded. Make the count-and-insert atomic, for example with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit.

The device limit check is a non-atomic count followed by an insert. Concurrent requests from different new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the number of devices exceeds deviceLimit. Make the check and insert atomic, for example with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit, or serialize the check and insert under a lock.

WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice does check-then-act (CountDevices then INSERT/UPSERT) with no lock, transaction, or unique-guard when deviceLimit>0. WHY: Two concurrent new-device requests can both observe count < limit and both insert, exceeding the configured limit and breaking the enforcement contract. HOW: Enforce atomically (e.g., conditional insert guarded by count in one statement/transaction with serializable lock, or re-check count on conflict).

issues.descricao: Device slots are keyed by the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header with no validation or rate limiting, so an anonymous caller can fill the limit with fake IDs and deny anonymous access to every new legitimate device.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Device slots counted toward deviceLimit are keyed by the unauthenticated X-Grafana-Device-Id header (read in impl.go TagDevice) with no validation or rate-limit. WHY: Any anonymous caller can mint arbitrary device IDs to fill the table up to the limit, after which all legitimate new anonymous devices get ErrDeviceLimitReached and authentication is denied — a trivial anonymous-access DoS introduced by the limit. HOW: Do not let a single client consume many slots (e.g., bind slot consumption to IP/fingerprint, rate-limit new-device creation, or require proof of distinct device).

issues.descricao: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit and never verifies that an existing device can still be updated at the limit.

comentarios.texto: The at-limit call reuses a brand-new device ID ("keep") that was never inserted, so it only reaches updateDevice's `rowsAffected == 0` -> ErrDeviceLimitReached branch. The success branch of the newly added updateDevice (an existing device still being updated while the store is at the limit) is never exercised by any test — every other call uses deviceLimit 0, so updateDevice is never invoked. A regression that made updateDevice always affect 0 rows, use a wrong WHERE/SET, or unconditionally return ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever limit>0 would leave this and all other tests green. Add a case that, after the store is at the limit, calls CreateOrUpdateDevice again with the SAME DeviceID and asserts require.NoError (and ideally that client_ip/user_agent/updated_at were changed), so the update path is actually verified.

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit. It would still pass if updateDevice always returned ErrDeviceLimitReached, because it never re-submits the existing device (DeviceID "32mdo31deeqwes") at the limit. Add a call that updates the existing device with a new UserAgent or UpdatedAt, require NoError, and check the stored row changed.

issues.descricao: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
issues.textoGolden: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TagDevice failures that triggered the new ErrDeviceLimitReached early-return are not permanent, because tagDeviceUI (impl.go:87) writes the device key into localCache BEFORE CreateOrUpdateDevice (impl.go:93) and never evicts it on error; tagDeviceUI returns early on any cache hit (impl.go:83-84). WHY: the first request from a new over-limit device is denied, but the poisoned cache makes every subsequent request from that same device skip the limit check entirely and authenticate successfully, so the configurable device limit is bypassed by simply retrying. HOW: only set the cache key after CreateOrUpdateDevice returns nil (e.g. move a.localCache.SetDefault after the successful DB write, or delete the key when it returns ErrDeviceLimitReached).

TagDevice now propagates ErrDeviceLimitReached to deny an over-limit anonymous device, but tagDeviceUI (impl.go:83-95) records the device in localCache at line 87 *before* calling a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store rejects the device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the key is already cached, so the next request for that same device returns early at line 83 with a nil error and the device is admitted. The limit therefore only blocks the first request and is silently bypassed on retry. Fix by only setting the cache entry after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds (move SetDefault after the store call), or by removing/not caching the key on failure.

The new authentication gate accepts retries from devices that were rejected by the limit because tagDeviceUI inserts the cache entry before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds. At capacity, the first request with a new X-Grafana-Device-Id fails, but subsequent requests with that same ID hit the 29-minute cache and receive an anonymous identity without admission to the device store. Cache only successful admissions, and ensure concurrent requests cannot treat an in-progress admission as successful.

issues.descricao: Device tagging now runs synchronously in Authenticate, adding DB round-trips on cache-miss anonymous requests where it used to be fire-and-forget.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Anonymous.Authenticate changed from fire-and-forget goroutine TagDevice to synchronous TagDevice(ctx) that runs CountDevices + INSERT/UPDATE inline. WHY: Every cache-miss anonymous authentication now blocks on two DB round-trips in the login hot path, adding latency and DB load per request where previously auth returned immediately. HOW: Restore async tagging for the non-limit path or at least decouple denial from the hot path (e.g., async count with cached count, or only synchronously enforce when near limit).

issues.descricao: The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

comentarios.texto: The new device_limit setting is read without adding a corresponding key to conf/defaults.ini. applyEnvVariableOverrides only visits keys already present in the loaded INI and runs before readAuthSettings, so setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone is ignored and leaves the limit at zero, disabling enforcement. Add an uncommented device_limit = 0 entry under auth.anonymous in defaults.ini so the standard environment override mechanism can apply it.

issues.descricao: The anonymous device limit is enforced only through TagDevice, which returns nil when the client-controlled device ID header is missing, so requests without the header authenticate anonymously regardless of the configured limit.

The doc comment on updateDevice says it updates a device "updated between the given times", but the function takes no times, computes the 30-day window itself and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when no row matches.
updateDevice prepends the query to the captured args inside the retried DB callback, so a SQLite lock retry runs Exec with the query duplicated in the arguments and the update fails.

sugestoes.texto: When `user_count` is an exact multiple of the limit (for example 50 users with a limit of 50), the pager shows "1/2" and Next stays enabled for an empty page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

`group.add` calls `users.push` even when the user is already a member, so it inserts a duplicate `group_users` row or hits the unique index and returns a 500. The old `usernames=` path diffed the lists to avoid this. Skip users who already belong to the group.

The old removal path (`destroy_deletions`) cleared `primary_group_id` for removed users; `users.delete(user_id)` does not, so removed users keep the group's title and flair. Use `group.remove(user)` and also clear `primary_group_id` when it points at this group.

Any visitor who can see a group can request `limit=1000000` and make the server load and serialize every member of a large automatic group (for example trust_level_0) in one request. Clamp `limit` to a small maximum such as 200.

`findMembers()` now asks for only 50 members (server default `limit` is also 50), but the public `group/members.hbs` has no pagination controls. On the public group page, every member after the first 50 is no longer reachable, while before this PR non-automatic groups listed everyone. Add next/previous controls to the public page, as the admin page has, or keep a full listing there.

issues.descricao: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
issues.textoGolden: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.

comentarios.texto: totalPages (and currentPage) use `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which is an off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members, limit 50 → reports 2 pages although only 1 exists). This leaves `showingLast` false on the real last page, so 'next' navigates to an empty page at offset=user_count. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (and compute currentPage consistently) to get the correct page count.

totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 for user_count=50, limit=50, although 50 members occupy exactly one page. Correct it to `Math.ceil(this.get('user_count') / this.get('limit'))`. Effect: for a group whose member count is a multiple of the page size, totalPages is one too high, showingLast remains false so the 'next' link stays enabled, and clicking it navigates to a phantom empty page.

`totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts by one whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members with limit 50 yields 2 pages instead of 1). Since `showingLast` is `propertyEqual("currentPage", "totalPages")`, on a full last page `showingLast` is false, so the `next` action stays enabled and advances `offset` to `user_count`, rendering an empty page labeled as the last page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the zero-member guard) so the count matches the real number of pages.

issues.descricao: Several Group model functions (findMembers, destroy, userCountDisplay) return a value on some paths and undefined on others, triggering consistent-return lint warnings.
issues.textoGolden: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

issues.descricao: Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.

comentarios.texto: Guard against stale member-fetch responses before updating the model. `next` updates offset immediately and leaves navigation enabled, so with at least three pages two rapid clicks issue requests for offsets 50 and 100. If the offset-100 response arrives first and the offset-50 response arrives last, this unconditional `setProperties` resets both offset and members to the older page, undoing the latest navigation. Refreshes after membership changes can similarly be overwritten by an earlier fetch. Track a per-model request generation and apply only the latest response, or serialize navigation and refresh requests.

issues.descricao: The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.

comentarios.texto: The public members route now loads only the model's default 50-member page without providing any way to request subsequent pages. The public group/members.hbs template only renders members and has no Next/Previous controls, so members after the first 50 become inaccessible (manual groups previously returned all members). Add public pagination controls and actions that update offset and reload members.

The new default limit applies to nonautomatic groups as well, but the public group-members route still calls findMembers() only once and its template simply iterates members without pagination. Previously this endpoint returned every member of a nonautomatic group; now a group with more than 50 members exposes only the first 50 on its public members page, with no way to reach the rest. Update that consumer to fetch subsequent pages or provide pagination when introducing this endpoint contract.

Provide pagination or load subsequent pages for the public group-members view. findMembers now requests only 50 members, and this route calls it only once while its template simply iterates members without navigation. Custom groups previously returned all members, so groups larger than 50 now have members that cannot be viewed on this page.

issues.descricao: Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.

comentarios.texto: Persist params[:alias_level] when creating a group, just as update does. The creation form exposes aliasLevelOptions and group.asJSON sends the selected alias_level, but create saves only name and visible. A newly created group therefore retains the default alias level instead of the administrator's selection.

issues.descricao: Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) instead of the Group#remove destroy path. WHY: bypasses GroupUser destroy callbacks and primary_group_id cleanup done in destroy_deletions, leaving stale membership side-effects (e.g. dangling primary_group_id). HOW: load the User and call group.remove(user).

Removing a member with group.users.delete bypasses the primary_group_id cleanup previously performed by Group#destroy_deletions during usernames updates. A user whose primary group is this group remains associated with it as their primary group after membership removal, leaving stale primary-group state used by user administration and post serialization. Clear primary_group_id for the removed user when it equals this group's id as part of the removal operation.

issues.descricao: The remove_member spec issues a PUT request although the route only maps DELETE to remove_member, so the test uses a verb never routed in production.
issues.textoGolden: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

comentarios.texto: This example sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the PR maps `remove_member` only to DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`); PUT on that path routes to `groups#add_members`. Controller specs bypass the router, so the example still lands on `remove_member` and passes regardless — it would still pass if the DELETE route were missing or wired to the wrong action, leaving the newly introduced verb/action pairing untested. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member`, as the sibling example at line 125 already does.

The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. It exercises the action with a verb that is never routed in production. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` so the test matches the real request.

issues.descricao: Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
`add_members` runs one User query per username; load all users with a single `User.where(username: ...)` query.

sugestoes.texto: This call passes an empty `data` object to `updateMany`. Prisma has no column to write, so `@updatedAt` may never change and the 'last updated' status the PR depends on stays stale. Set the timestamp explicitly, for example `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`.

The handler throws a plain `Error` when the credential is missing or belongs to someone else. tRPC turns that into an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) instead of a NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN error the client can handle. Throw a `TRPCError` with code `NOT_FOUND` instead.

GNU sed reads the `''` after `-i` as the script and fails, so on Linux the script never updates `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` in an existing `.env`. Use a portable form, for example `sed -i.bak ... && rm "$ENV_FILE.bak"`.

Callers like `EventAdvancedTab` don't pass the optional `onChanged`, so after a cache delete the `connectedCalendars` query is never refetched and the dropdown keeps showing the old cache timestamp and the delete action. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in this mutation's `onSettled`, the same way `disconnectMutation` already does.

issues.descricao: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId with an empty data object, so Prisma does not refresh the @updatedAt timestamp and SelectedCalendar.updatedAt never reflects the cache refresh.
issues.textoGolden: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {} to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. WHY: Prisma updateMany rejects empty data (validation error) or no-ops without touching @updatedAt, so the refresh path throws or silently leaves updatedAt stale. HOW: pass an explicit touch field e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() }.

Comment claims "Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt" but call passes empty object {} as data, so nothing is updated (Prisma updateMany with empty data is a no-op/error). Fix comment or pass { updatedAt: new Date() } to match the stated intent.

updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {}. Prisma updateMany throws when data is empty, so this line throws on every resync after the cache write. Pass an explicit touch e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() } instead of {}.

issues.descricao: After deleting the calendar cache, CredentialActionsDropdown does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, so where no parent refetch callback is passed the stale cache status and delete action remain visible.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `deleteCacheMutation`'s `onSuccess` only calls `onSuccess?.()` and never invalidates the `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query, while the sibling `disconnectMutation` explicitly invalidates it in `onSettled`. WHY: the 'Cache Status' row in the dropdown is rendered from the cached `connectedCalendars` result; after deleting the cache the query is not refetched, so the deleted status/last-updated entry stays visible and stale in the UI. HOW: invalidate the query in the cache-deletion mutation as well, e.g. `const utils = trpc.useUtils(); onSuccess: async () => { ...; await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate(); }`.

WHAT: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only calls onSuccess?.() and never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike disconnectMutation onSettled. WHY: cacheUpdatedAt stays stale after deletion so UI keeps showing old Last updated and delete action until manual refetch. HOW: add onSettled invalidate of connectedCalendars like disconnect does.

Successful cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper forwards only an optional parent onChanged callback and disables window-focus refetch, so the deleted cache continues to appear present with its old timestamp and delete action. Invalidate utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on successful deletion.

issues.descricao: The cache 'last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded en-US locale instead of the user's locale, so non-US users see US-style dates in an otherwise translated label.
issues.textoGolden: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

comentarios.texto: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded "en-US" locale (new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)), so every user — regardless of their locale — sees a US-style date/time while the surrounding label is translated. Use the app's locale-aware date formatting helper (the user's current locale) instead of pinning en-US.

Date format hard-coded to "en-US" via Intl.DateTimeFormat while surrounding strings use t()/useLocale. Users in other locales see US short date/time. Use the active locale from useLocale/i18n instead of hard-coding "en-US".

The cache timestamp is always formatted with "en-US", even though the surrounding label uses the user's selected translation locale. Users in other locales therefore see US month/day ordering and time conventions inside an otherwise localized message, potentially misreading the last-update date. Use the active application locale for Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of hard-coding en-US.

issues.descricao: The calendar cache migration keeps a generated warning saying updatedAt has no default and cannot be added to a non-empty table, although the SQL adds it with DEFAULT NOW().

comentarios.texto: This warning says updatedAt is added without a default and cannot be added to a nonempty table, but the migration actually supplies DEFAULT NOW(), explicitly handling existing rows. Remove or correct the warning so operators reviewing the migration are not incorrectly told that existing data makes it unsafe to run.

issues.descricao: The test-gcal-webhooks.sh cleanup function always exits 0, including when called from the failure paths, so the script reports success when the tunnel could not be set up.

comentarios.texto: `cleanup` always runs `exit 0`, and it is also called on the failure paths (rate limit hit, failed to extract the URL). The script therefore reports success even though the tunnel failed and GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was never updated. Have `cleanup` take an exit code, and pass 1 from the failure paths.

cleanup() always ends in `exit 0`, and both failure paths (rate-limit at lines 46-50 and 'Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL' at lines 56-59) call cleanup. So a script named test-gcal-webhooks that did not actually obtain the tunnel URL / update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL still exits with status 0, letting any automation treat the run as successful even though the setup it verifies failed. On the failure branches the script should exit non-zero (e.g. `exit 1`) so failure is observable; only the SIGINT/SIGTERM interactive shutdown should exit 0.

issues.descricao: The webhook test script updates .env with the macOS-only `sed -i ''` syntax, which fails on Linux GNU sed and leaves GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged.
issues.textoGolden: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `sed -i '' -E 's|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|...|' "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD/macOS `sed -i ''` form. WHY: under GNU sed (typical Linux dev/CI environment) the empty `''` is consumed as the script operand and the command errors, so the existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` line is never replaced and the tunnel URL is not written to the env file. HOW: use a portable invocation, e.g. `sed -i.bak -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"` (or branch on `uname`).

The environment update uses BSD sed's `-i ''` syntax, which fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the script leaves the previous URL unchanged but still prints that it was updated, preventing webhooks from reaching the new tunnel. Use a portable replacement strategy or select the in-place syntax based on the available sed implementation and check its exit status.

When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, `sed -i ''` uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails under GNU sed on Linux. The script nevertheless prints that the URL was updated and keeps the tunnel running, leaving webhooks configured with the old URL. Use a portable replacement approach (or select the appropriate sed syntax) and only announce success after the edit succeeds.

issues.descricao: deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error when the credential is missing or not owned by the user, so tRPC returns a 500 instead of a structured FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND error.
issues.textoGolden: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.

issues.descricao: connectedCalendarsHandler instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly instead of the feature-flag-aware factory, so cache status is queried and shown even when calendar-cache is disabled.
The dev script writes tunnelmole output to a fixed /tmp/tmole.log, so a local attacker's symlink at that path could make it overwrite an arbitrary file.

The new test-gcal-webhooks.sh writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL to '../.env' relative to the current directory, so running it from the repo root creates/edits a .env above the repo and the app never sees the URL.

sugestoes.texto: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the logged-in user has never had a TopicUser row for this topic, for example when someone opens a forwarded or shared unsubscribe link. `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500. The same failure happens if `notification_level` itself is nil. Use `TopicUser.change`, or handle the missing row and nil level by defaulting to regular, so the update also publishes the MessageBus notification.

Any third-party page can embed `/t/x/<id>/unsubscribe` (for example as an img tag) and silently change notification levels for a logged-in victim, because GET requests skip CSRF checks. The action also lowers the level again on each hit, so a reload or mail-client link prefetch takes a Watching topic down to Muted. Make the GET request show only a confirmation page and apply the change through an authenticated POST/PUT, or require a signed per-user token in the URL.

Saving `notification_level` directly skips the work `TopicUser.change` does on every level change: it leaves `notifications_reason_id` (for example auto_watch) and `notifications_changed_at` unchanged, and it never publishes `notification_level_change` on MessageBus. As a result, the topic can show the wrong notification reason, and other open sessions keep showing the old level. Call `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id].to_i, notification_level: new_level)` instead of `tu.save!`.

issues.descricao: The new unsubscribe endpoint changes the user's topic notification level on a plain GET request, so a third-party page can trigger it for a logged-in user without any CSRF token.

comentarios.texto: The unsubscribe endpoint mutates notification_level (tu.save!) via a plain GET route (config/routes.rb:440-441) with skip_before_filter :check_xhr, authenticating only through the session cookie. There is no CSRF token (Rails forgery protection does not cover GET) and no capability token, unlike EmailController#unsubscribe which authorizes via DigestUnsubscribeKey. Any third-party page can embed and, when a logged-in user loads it, silently change that user's notification_level for the topic. Require a per-user capability token (like the digest unsubscribe key) in the URL, or perform the state change from an authenticated non-GET request that carries the CSRF token.

The new GET routes mutate the authenticated user's notification preferences without CSRF verification. An attacker can navigate a logged-in user's browser to a known topic unsubscribe URL and reduce or mute its notifications, because Rails excludes GET from forgery-token checks and unsubscribe explicitly skips check_xhr. Make GET render a confirmation page and perform the preference change through a CSRF-protected POST or PUT.

WHAT: The unsubscribe state change (lowering/muting notification_level + save!) runs on a GET route (config/routes.rb GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe). WHY: An attacker can forge the URL as an image/prefetch/link to silently change a victim's notification state with no CSRF token since GETs are not CSRF-protected. HOW: Make the mutation a PUT/POST with CSRF protection or require an explicit confirmation parameter/token instead of mutating on page view.

issues.descricao: TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences TopicUser.find_by without handling a missing row, so users with no topic_users record get a NoMethodError/500 instead of being unsubscribed.
issues.textoGolden: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash

comentarios.texto: tu is not checked for nil before use. TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) returns nil whenever the logged-in user has no topic_users row for that topic (the same lookup TopicUser.get performs), and the next line dereferences tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. Because the route is only gated by ensure_logged_in, any logged-in user can hit /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe(.json) for a topic they never opened and trigger the crash. Guard the lookup, e.g. `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...); return render json: {success: false} unless tu` (or build/return early) before reading notification_level.

`TopicUser.find_by(...)` can return nil (e.g. the user clicks the emailed unsubscribe link for a topic for which no TopicUser row was ever created), and the very next line dereferences it (`tu.notification_level > ...`, then `tu.save!`). This raises NoMethodError on nil and the unsubscribe request 500s. Guard the nil case (e.g. return early or use `TopicUser.change`/`find_or_create_by`) before reading/writing notification_level.

`tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (find_by yields nil when no row exists), but the next lines dereference it unconditionally (`tu.notification_level`, `tu.save!`). Since the new unsubscribe routes are public GET endpoints, any logged-in user visiting /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe for a topic they have never tracked will trigger a NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a sane response. Guard the nil case (e.g. create/skip or redirect) before reading notification_level.

issues.descricao: The message builder spec passes unsubscribe_url in the fixture but never asserts the per-topic unsubscribe link appears in the email.

comentarios.texto: The `unsubscribe_url` added to the `message_with_unsubscribe` fixture is never asserted. The two tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header `be_present` and that the body matches `user_preferences_url`; neither references `unsubscribe_url`. So they would still pass if the topic-specific unsubscribe URL this PR introduces were dropped or wired to the wrong value. Add an assertion (e.g. that `message_with_unsubscribe.body` matches `/t/1234/unsubscribe`, and that the List-Unsubscribe header points at the topic unsubscribe URL) so the new behaviour is actually covered.

The fixture now passes unsubscribe_url, but no assertion reads it. The tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header is present and that the body contains user_preferences_url, so they pass if the topic unsubscribe link is removed or broken. Add an assertion that the body includes "/t/1234/unsubscribe".

issues.descricao: The unsubscribe confirmation says the user will stop receiving notifications for the topic, but watching/tracking users are only moved to regular, which still sends mention/reply notifications.

comentarios.texto: The confirmation promises that the user will stop receiving notifications for this topic, but TopicsController#unsubscribe sets watching/tracking users to regular, not muted. Regular still allows mention/reply notifications, so this confirmation (and the corresponding promise in the new email link text) overstates what clicking the link accomplished. Describe stopping notifications for every new post, or make the confirmation conditional on the resulting notification level so only muted users are told that all topic notifications have stopped.

issues.descricao: Unsubscribe saves the new notification level without setting notifications_reason_id, so auto-tracked topics are promoted back to tracking on the next read, undoing the unsubscribe.

comentarios.texto: Saving the notification level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged instead of recording an explicit user choice. For automatically tracked topics with a null reason, TopicUser.update_last_read promotes the row back to tracking when the reading threshold is exceeded, undoing the unsubscribe on the next read. Persist the change through TopicUser.change so notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at are set consistently with set_notifications.

Saving the notification level directly bypasses the explicit-user-change metadata set by TopicUser.change. In particular, a topic_user with notifications_reason_id == nil remains eligible for TopicUser.auto_track, which checks that field and can promote the topic back to tracking after the user unsubscribes. Use the notification-change helper (or set its user-change reason and timestamp consistently) so the unsubscribe is retained as an explicit user preference.

issues.descricao: Claims the client unsubscribe route never performs the unsubscribe when entered through an in-app transition.

comentarios.texto: The client unsubscribe route only loads the ordinary topic view and never performs the unsubscribe operation. When entered through an in-app transition rather than a full server navigation, PostStream.loadTopicView requests /t/:id.json (or consumes preload data), so the page claims notifications will stop while the persisted notification level remains unchanged. Ensure this entry path executes the unsubscribe operation before showing confirmation.

The client route loads the topic but never invokes the unsubscribe action. Notification levels are changed only by TopicsController#unsubscribe, so navigating to this route inside the Ember application can display “You will stop receiving notifications” without changing the subscription. Explicitly perform the unsubscribe operation on client-side entry rather than relying on the initial HTML request to have done it.

issues.descricao: The property name stopNotificiationsText is misspelled (should be stopNotificationsText).
issues.textoGolden: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

issues.descricao: The topic unsubscribe GET endpoint is not idempotent: each visit steps the notification level down again, so reloading the link moves a topic from regular to muted.

sugestoes.texto: Line 73 checks `grantType` a second time under the `rawTokenId` message, so a null `rawTokenId` is never rejected and gets encoded as a token id ending in ":null". Pass `rawTokenId` to the second `requireNonNull` call.

The encoder writes the grant shortcut at characters 4–6, but the matcher reads `substring(3,5)`. It also returns false when the shortcut matches. For an id like "onrtac:<uuid>" it compares "ta" against "ac", so every test using `isAccessTokenId` passes no matter which grant type the token has. Use `substring(4, 6)` and return false when the shortcut does not match.

issues.descricao: The AccessTokenContext constructor checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId passes validation and is encoded as ':null'.
issues.textoGolden: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the constructor validates `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId` (`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`). WHY: a null `rawTokenId` is silently accepted, so `encodeTokenId` produces a token id ending in `:null` and any later consumer of the raw id gets an invalid value instead of an early failure. HOW: change the argument to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

Line 73 calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") — it validates grantType a second time (line 72 already does) with a message naming a different field. rawTokenId is never validated, so a null rawTokenId is accepted at construction and the advertised check/message is wrong. It should be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").

The null-check message names the wrong parameter: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` validates `grantType` but reports `rawTokenId`, and it duplicates the check on line 72 while `rawTokenId` is never validated at all. The message that reaches the reader contradicts the code it guards; it should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

issues.descricao: isAccessTokenId reads the grant shortcut at the wrong offset (3,5 instead of 4,6) and inverts the comparison, so the event assertions never verify the token's grant type.
issues.textoGolden: In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `isAccessTokenId` reads the grant shortcut from the wrong offset and inverts the comparison — `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. WHY: for the encoded id `ssttgg:raw` the grant shortcut occupies 0-based indices 4-5, so `substring(3,5)` inspects the token-type/grant boundary and can never equal the expected shortcut; combined with the inverted `return false`, the equality branch is unreachable and the matcher validates only the UUID part. As a result the new assertions in `expectCodeToToken`/`expectRefresh`/`expectDeviceCodeToToken`/`expectAuthReqIdToToken` do not actually assert the grant type and would pass even if the grant shortcut were wrong. HOW: use `items[0].substring(4, 6)` and negate the condition (`if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`).

The matcher logic is inverted: line 483 returns false when the extracted grant shortcut EQUALS expectedGrantShortcut, so a token that actually carries the expected grant fails the matcher, while a token with any other grant shortcut falls through and passes. The condition should be negated: `if (!items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Also note the encode site writes the grant shortcut at chars 4-6 (substring(4,6)); substring(3,5) reads one character early into the token-type field, so the offset is off by one relative to TokenManager.encodeTokenId.

The comment 'Grant type shortcut starts at character 4th char' disagrees with the encoding that this PR defines (sessionType chars 1-2, tokenType 3-4, grantType 5-6, e.g. 'trltcc'), and the code reads substring(3,5) — the 4th-5th chars, i.e. the token-type second char plus the grant first char, never the grant shortcut. The comment (and the index) should point at the 5th char / substring(4,6).

issues.descricao: getShortcut() Javadoc says shortcuts are usually 3 letters, but the encoding requires exactly 2-character shortcuts.
issues.textoGolden: Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.

comentarios.texto: The Javadoc says getShortcut() returns 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but every implementation introduced in this PR returns a 2-character shortcut ('ac','cc','pg','pc','rt','ro','te','ci','dg') and the encoder relies on exactly 2 chars (encoded context length 6 = 2+2+2). The doc states a length the code does not produce; it should say 2-character shortcut.

Grant shortcuts are registered without enforcing the two-character length required by the decoder. A custom grant returning a three-character shortcut, which the new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory documentation explicitly suggests, produces a seven-character prefix that getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects, breaking encode/decode round trips for that grant. Validate shortcut length during registration and dynamic refresh, and document the required two-character format.

The new contract describes getShortcut() as usually returning a three-letter shortcut, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires exactly two characters for the grant field (six total prefix characters, decoded with substring(4, 6)). An extension author following this documentation can produce token IDs that the default decoder rejects. Document the required two-character length rather than advertising three letters.

issues.descricao: testIncorrectGrantType catches any RuntimeException, so it passes on a NullPointerException from the unset sessionFactory rather than verifying the unknown-grant IllegalArgumentException.
issues.textoGolden: Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

comentarios.texto: Catching RuntimeException allows this negative test to pass for an unrelated fixture failure. The fixture constructs the factory without postInit, leaving sessionFactory null; resolving the unregistered `ac` shortcut calls sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream and throws NullPointerException before the decoder's intended unknown-grant IllegalArgumentException. Catch/assert IllegalArgumentException specifically and provide a factory fixture whose lookup returns no matching grant, so removing the decoder's validation would fail the test.

issues.descricao: Client-credentials (and UMA permission) token issuance never sets the GRANT_TYPE attribute, so their access token ids are encoded with the unknown grant 'na' instead of their shortcut.

comentarios.texto: The new grant metadata falls back to 'na' for client-credentials and UMA tokens because their issuance paths never set Constants.GRANT_TYPE on their fresh ClientSessionContext. ClientCredentialsGrantType calls responseBuilder.generateAccessToken directly, and PermissionGrantType delegates to AuthorizationTokenService, so neither executes the new assignment in createTokenResponse; tokens from these known grants therefore carry unknown grant context. Set the grant attribute in both issuance paths before generating the access token.

issues.descricao: Lazy registration of newly deployed grants does not check shortcut uniqueness, so a grant reusing an existing shortcut silently overwrites the reverse mapping and older tokens decode to the wrong grant.

comentarios.texto: Enforce shortcut uniqueness during lazy registration rather than overwriting grantsByShortcuts. If a newly deployed grant B uses existing grant A's shortcut, this path replaces shortcut→A with shortcut→B while retaining both forward entries. Previously issued A tokens then decode as B. Concurrent registrations of two new grants with the same shortcut likewise both succeed, with the last inverse-map write winning. Use collision-aware atomic registration and reject the conflicting grant before publishing its forward mapping.

issues.descricao: getShortcut() is added as an abstract method to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default, breaking existing custom grant type factories (compile error or AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls it).

sugestoes.texto: If one SendGrid request throws (for example, a 400 for a batch already cancelled), the whole try block exits. Later reminders are never cancelled, and none of the queued `delete` promises are awaited, so the same failing row blocks every cron run until line 34 deletes the reminders after their scheduledDate passes. By then SendGrid has sent emails for cancelled or rescheduled bookings. Wrap each reminder in its own try/catch and delete each row right after its cancel succeeds.

The old code pushed the reminder DB deletes into `prismaPromises` and awaited them. Now the async helpers run fire-and-forget, so in a serverless handler the `cancelled: true` update or SMS delete may never finish, and the reminder is still sent. The same pattern appears in `handleNewBooking` (lines 966-972, where try/catch cannot catch async rejections), `bookings.tsx` and `workflows.tsx`. Collect the returned promises and await them.

Callers used to delete the row on their own, but now the helper deletes it only after `cancelSMS` succeeds. A Twilio error (for example, a message already sent) leaves an orphaned reminder row tied to a cancelled booking. Catch the Twilio error separately so the DB delete always runs.

issues.descricao: Reminder cancel helpers are called without await inside forEach when bookings are cancelled/rescheduled or workflows edited, so the handler can return before reminders are cancelled or deleted and failures are unobserved.
issues.textoGolden: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder called inside forEach without collecting/awaiting promises. WHY: handler returns before cancels complete and rejections are unobserved, so cancellations are lost and reminder emails/SMS are still sent (same fire-and-forget pattern repeated in handleNewBooking:966, bookings.tsx:488, workflows.tsx:212/376/519/574).

Cancellation now delegates the database update/deletion to asynchronous reminder helpers without awaiting them, while removing reminder deletes from the awaited promise list. The handler can finish before cancelled flags or unscheduled-reminder deletions are persisted, allowing a subsequent scheduler run to schedule a cancelled booking's reminder and leaving cancellation work unfinished when a serverless invocation terminates. Collect and await the helper promises; apply the same correction to the modified rescheduling and workflow-update callers that discard these promises.

Await the reminder cancellation promises before completing the cancellation request. These helpers now own persistence of cancellation: email awaits a workflowReminder update and SMS awaits Twilio before deleting the row. The forEach discards their promises, and removing remindersToDelete from the awaited promise list removes the previous guarantee that reminder state is cleared before the handler returns. In a serverless request the outstanding operations can be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect these helper promises and include them in the awaited Promise.all.

issues.descricao: The cron cancels SendGrid sends for cancelled reminders in one try around the whole loop, so one failing cancel aborts all remaining cancellations and the row deletions, and the failing row blocks later runs.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remindersToCancel loop awaits SendGrid cancel per-reminder inside one try and only runs Prisma deletes after the loop, with no method filter. WHY: a single throw (e.g. null SMS referenceId sent as batch_id, or one SendGrid error) aborts the loop and skips Promise.all deletes, leaving all other cancelled emails still scheduled so they are still sent.

Successful cancellation records are only deleted after every SendGrid request in the loop succeeds. If a later request fails, the catch skips all queued Prisma deletions; the next run retries an already-cancelled batch, which SendGrid rejects with 400, and aborts before processing the remaining reminders. Await each reminder's database deletion immediately after its successful cancellation and isolate errors per reminder so one failed batch does not block the others.

Handle cancellation failures per reminder rather than around the entire batch. If one SendGrid request rejects (for example, for an expired or invalid batch ID), the loop exits before cancelling the remaining reminders, and Promise.all is never reached, so even earlier successfully cancelled reminders remain in the database. The failed record stays eligible for the next run and can repeatedly block other cancellations until their emails are sent. Execute each successful deletion and isolate failures so the worker continues processing the remaining reminders.

issues.descricao: Email reminders for cancelled bookings are only flagged cancelled and cancelled in SendGrid by the cron later, so reminders close to their send time can still be delivered.

comentarios.texto: Deferred cancellation includes reminders less than ten minutes from their scheduled send time, when SendGrid no longer permits cancellation. A booking cancelled in that interval is only marked cancelled locally by deleteScheduledEmailReminder, and the cron's POST is rejected, so its email is still delivered. Process cancellation before SendGrid's ten-minute cutoff and explicitly handle cancellations that arrive after that deadline rather than relying on this cron query to stop delivery.

issues.descricao: The cron cancels SendGrid scheduled sends one at a time with sequential awaits, which is slower than batching.

comentarios.texto: The new cancel loop performs a sequentially awaited SendGrid HTTP request (`await client.request(...)`) for each reminder returned by an unbounded `findMany` (no `take`), then deletes them. WHY: this is O(N) serial network round-trips per cron run; if many reminders are cancelled at once (e.g. a bulk event-type disable or booking cancellation wave) the cron handler can block for a long time on serial SendGrid latency. HOW: fan the independent SendGrid cancel requests out with `Promise.all`, and/or bound the query with `take` plus pagination, then batch the DB deletes.

WHAT: SendGrid cancel issued with sequential await inside for loop over remindersToCancel. WHY: cron blocks O(N) sequential network round-trips instead of parallel batch, materially slowing the hourly schedule job as cancelled backlog grows.

issues.descricao: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and its immediateDelete flag do not delete anything; the names no longer describe the behaviour.

comentarios.texto: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and its `immediateDelete` flag no longer match what the code does. The default path only marks the reminder `cancelled: true`, and the `immediateDelete` path only sends a cancel request to the email provider. Neither path deletes the scheduled send or the row, unlike the SMS counterpart, which still deletes. Rename them (for example `cancelScheduledEmailReminder` and `immediateCancel`) or document the behaviour.

issues.descricao: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the DB row only after a successful Twilio cancel, so a cancel failure leaves the reminder row behind now that callers no longer delete it.

comentarios.texto: twilio.cancelSMS and prisma.workflowReminder.delete share one try block. If the Twilio cancel throws, the DB row is never deleted. The reminder row then stays behind for a booking that was cancelled, rescheduled or deleted, because the callers no longer delete rows themselves. Delete the row in a finally block, or handle the cancel failure separately so the delete still runs.

issues.descricao: Prisma is imported in workflows.tsx but no longer used.

comentarios.texto: `Prisma` is imported as a value (line 9) but is no longer used anywhere in this file. This PR removed the only usages (`Prisma.BatchPayload` in the now-deleted `remindersToDelete` / `deleteReminderPromise` declarations), while the import was kept. WHY: the repo's ESLint `no-unused-vars` rule will fail CI/build for an unused import. HOW: remove `Prisma` from the import list (and keep `import type { PrismaPromise }` as a type-only import).

issues.descricao: The cron route sets the API key only on @sendgrid/mail, so the new @sendgrid/client cancellation requests are unauthenticated and reminders for cancelled bookings stay scheduled.

sugestoes.texto: Keycloak previously stored only hashed recovery codes, but `createRecoveryCodesCredential` now passes the raw codes as JSON to `updateCredential`, so any federated provider that supports the type receives the plaintext backup codes. The test provider in this PR stores them and compares them in plaintext. If an external store leaks or is read, every MFA backup code is exposed. Pass the hashed `credentialModel` data (e.g. `credentialModel.getSecretData()`) instead of the raw `generatedCodes`.

`getMyUser` returns null for usernames missing from the in-memory map, and every other method in the class checks for that. The new `getCredentials` reads `myUser.recoveryCodes` right away, so loading federated credentials for an unknown user throws a `NullPointerException`. Return `Stream.empty()` when `myUser` is null.

When the recovery-codes credential comes from user storage, the used code is never consumed and `removeStoredCredentialById` targets the local database, which does not hold that id (the test provider's `createFromValues` model has no id at all). As a result `allCodesUsed()` never becomes true, the codes can be reused, and `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` is never added. Mark used codes and delete the credential through the user-storage credential API (for example `disableCredentialType` or `updateCredential`) when the credential is from user storage, and keep `removeStoredCredentialById` only for local credentials.

issues.descricao: The test user-storage provider validates recovery codes without consuming the used code, so the same code can be replayed.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The new recovery-codes branch of isValid only checks whether the submitted code appears in the stored list and never removes the consumed entry. WHY: Unlike the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid (which calls removeRecoveryAuthnCode()+updateStoredCredential), the federated path never consumes a code and allCodesUsed() can never become true, so a used recovery code remains valid and can be replayed indefinitely. HOW: On a successful match, remove that entry from the stored codes (rewrite recoveryCodes.credentialData), mirroring the local provider's consume-on-success semantics.

The new recovery-code validator accepts any code in the original list without consuming the accepted code. Repeating a successful login with the same code succeeds indefinitely, while getCredentials reconstructs all original codes so the login form never advances or detects exhaustion. Validate the next unused code and persist its consumption before returning success.

The new federated recovery-code validator accepts any code in the original list but never removes a successfully used code from myUser.recoveryCodes. Consequently the same recovery code remains valid on subsequent logins, and getCredentials reconstructs the full original set every time. Consume and persist the successfully validated code (and test a second login/replay), so federated recovery codes retain their one-time semantics.

issues.descricao: getCredentials rebuilds the recovery-codes credential without copying the stored credential id, so the returned federated credential has a null id and cannot be targeted by id-based removal.
issues.textoGolden: After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: getCredentials builds the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel via createFromValues but never sets its id from the stored myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() (createFromValues does not populate id). WHY: The returned federated model has a null id, so callers that identify/delete the credential by id — e.g. RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()) when all codes are used, or federated-credential deletion via getFederatedCredentialsStream — cannot target the actual credential. HOW: call model.setId(myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()) after createFromValues.

getCredentials rebuilds the recovery-code model without copying the ID assigned during updateCredential. createFromValues does not assign an ID, so the exposed federated credential has a null ID and CredentialDeleteHelper cannot resolve it by the stored credential ID for account deletion. Copy myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() to the reconstructed model before returning it.

The CredentialModel returned from getCredentials for recovery codes is built with createFromValues and never gets the stored credential's id (myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()). RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator later calls removeStoredCredentialById(model.getId()) once all codes are used, and this would pass a null id. Fix: call model.setId(myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()) after creating the model.

issues.descricao: Creating recovery codes in external storage does not remove a previously stored local recovery-codes credential, and validation falls back to local storage, so the replaced codes still authenticate.

comentarios.texto: Successful recovery-code creation in external storage leaves any existing locally stored recovery-code credential active. For a federated user who previously stored codes locally and now has an external provider supporting this type, regeneration no longer calls RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential's replacement cleanup; UserCredentialManager.isValid falls back to the local validator when external validation rejects an old code, so the supposedly replaced codes still authenticate. Remove the previous local recovery-code credential after successful external creation.

issues.descricao: Exhausted recovery codes are removed with removeStoredCredentialById, which only covers local storage, so a federated recovery-codes credential is never removed.

comentarios.texto: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() can now return a credential from user storage (federated), but this code still calls removeStoredCredentialById() on it once all codes are used. That removal only targets local stored credentials, so a federated credential may not be removed. The user could then be left with an exhausted credential in user storage. Remove federated credentials through the federated path, or confirm the removal reaches user storage.

RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can now return a credential from user storage, but exhausted codes are cleaned up with removeStoredCredentialById, which only targets the local DB. For a federated credential (possibly with a null id), the exhausted credential is never removed or the call misbehaves, so the user keeps a dead credential. Remove federated credentials through a path that covers user storage, for example by checking where the credential came from.

RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can now return a federated credential. The authenticator still removes an exhausted one with removeStoredCredentialById(getId()), which only deletes from the local store, and the federated model's id may be null. Remove the credential through the path that matches where it was found, for example by checking whether it came from the federated stream and using the federated removal.

issues.descricao: Looking up recovery codes now always queries the federated provider first, which for LDAP users adds an LDAP round-trip and can throw IllegalStateException, failing recovery-code login with a 500.
An error log in the test user storage hard-codes the credential type as 'recovery-codes' instead of using RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE ('recovery-authn-codes').

The test federation provider BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage regenerates the recovery-codes model from the raw list on every getCredentials and never records consumed codes, so the next-code number and allCodesUsed() never reflect usage for its users.

sugestoes.texto: `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, so `Detector.detector_handler` raises `TypeError` for every `metric_alert_fire` detector when it calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`. That exception is not caught and aborts `process_detectors` for every detector in the packet. Before this change the handler was concrete and `evaluate` returned an empty result. Add stub implementations of the abstract members, or keep a concrete `DetectorHandler` until the real logic exists.

issues.descricao: The TODO above MetricAlertDetectorHandler says it will become a stateful detector, but the class already subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler.

comentarios.texto: The comment 'TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction' is now stale. MetricAlertDetectorHandler already subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler. Remove or reword the TODO.

Remove or revise the adjacent TODO saying this will become a stateful detector 'when we build that abstraction'. The class now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler, so the comment describes already-completed work as a future migration and misleads maintainers about which abstraction this handler uses.

issues.descricao: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.
issues.textoGolden: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty body, so it does not implement the abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data declared on StatefulDetectorHandler. WHY: the class is now abstract, and Detector.detector_handler (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) instantiates it via group_type.detector_handler(self), so any detector whose type resolves to this grouptype will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler — the previous version implemented evaluate and was instantiable. HOW: implement the required abstract methods (or keep a concrete evaluate override) so the handler can be constructed.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but with `pass`, so it implements none of the abstract methods it inherits (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data). The class is therefore still abstract and instantiating it (it is registered as `detector_handler` on MetricAlertFire and is constructed by Detector.detector_handler) raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`. Before this change it subclassed DetectorHandler and implemented the single abstract `evaluate`, so it was instantiable; the PR makes the metric-alert handler path throw. Either implement the required abstract methods or keep the class free of unimplemented abstracts.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler (an abc.ABC) with only `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares four abstract methods — counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data (detector.py:142-170) — none of which are implemented here. issues.descricao: The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.
issues.textoGolden: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.

comentarios.texto: The new occurrence builder accepts `value` but never incorporates or asserts it, so the occurrence tests cannot detect incorrect forwarding of the measured value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. For example, `test_state_results_multi_group` supplies 10 for group_2 but builds its expected occurrence with 6 and still passes. A regression that passes a constant or another group's measurement at the new production hook would therefore go unnoticed. Include the value in the mock occurrence's evidence and use the actual expected measurement, or assert the hook's arguments directly.

`build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value: int` but never uses it (the occurrence is built only from `group_key`/`new_status`), and this same helper is also the implementation of `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Because neither the expected occurrence nor the handler output depends on the value, tests like `test_state_results_multi_group` (which incorrectly builds the group_2 occurrence with `value=6` while the packet carries `10`) and `TestEvaluate.test_dedupe` (expected built with 6 vs packet 8) pass regardless of the value actually passed into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. If evaluation passed a wrong value, these tests would still pass, so they do not verify the value/threshold path they appear to cover. Include `value` in a field of the occurrence (or assert on it in the handler) and fix the wrong expected values so the argument is actually checked.

`build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts a `value: int` parameter but never uses it — the returned IssueOccurrence is derived only from `group_key` and `new_status`. Because `value` is dead, callers can pass a mismatched value with no failure: in `test_state_results_multi_group` the packet contains `group_2: 10`, but the expected occurrence for `group_2` is built with `6`. Either use `value` when constructing the occurrence so the test validates the group value, or drop the unused parameter and pass the correct value; otherwise the test silently accepts wrong group values.

sugestoes.texto: With the lock now covering only the cache write, `init`'s errgroup workers build indexes truly in parallel, and each one writes the shared outer `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` without synchronization (search.go:189-190). A worker that succeeds can overwrite another worker's error, or the race can corrupt it, and the race detector will flag it. In the `group.Go` closure, use a local `err :=` and update the counter with `atomic`.

`Stop()` still sets `s.initErr = "service is stopping"`, but the handlers no longer call `s.Init`, so nothing reads that field. A stopped server keeps accepting writes and reads against a backend that has already been shut down. Check `s.initErr` (or a stopped flag) at the start of each handler, or drop the dead assignment in `Stop`.

When `Init` fails inside the constructor, the server is thrown away but `cancel()` is never called, and `lifecycle.Init` (which already ran) is never paired with `Stop`. Backend pollers and goroutines started there leak for the lifetime of the process. On this error path, call `cancel()` and `s.lifecycle.Stop`.

issues.descricao: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.
issues.textoGolden: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Removing the function-wide `b.cacheMu.Lock()/defer Unlock()` and keeping only the lock around `b.cache[key]=idx` removes the only thing that serialized GetIndex against an in-flight build. WHY: getOrCreateIndex (resource/search.go:287-307) does GetIndex -> if nil -> build; previously BuildIndex held the write lock for its whole body so a concurrent caller's GetIndex (RLock) blocked until the first build cached the index and then saw it (no second build). Now GetIndex can return nil while a build for the same key is still running, so two requests/watch events build the SAME key concurrently — producing two distinct index instances where the caller holding the non-cached one never observes later writes (stale search results), and, for file-backed indices (size > FileThreshold), two concurrent `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` opening the same on-disk directory. HOW: guard the build per key (e.g. re-check the cache under the write lock after acquiring it, or use a per-key single-flight/lock so only one build runs per NamespacedResource), rather than relying on a global write lock held for the entire body.

The cache mutex was moved to cover only the cache assignment, removing the serialization that previously surrounded the whole BuildIndex. Two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key can now both construct an index (including `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same on-disk path) and both write `b.cache[key]`; the second overwrites the first, so callers get distinct index instances for one key and writes made through the losing instance are invisible to readers of the cached one (and the file-backed build may collide on the same directory). Keep the build for a given key serialized (e.g. restore the lock around the build, or take a per-key lock) instead of locking only the map write.

Locking only cache publication allows concurrent requests for the same uncached key to build separate indexes and overwrite each other's cache entries. Search and handleEvent both call getOrCreateIndex, whose GetIndex previously blocked behind the build-wide lock; now an event can update one newly built index before another build replaces it, losing that update from subsequent search results and leaving the discarded index open. Serialize builds per NamespacedResource and recheck the cache after acquiring that per-key guard.

issues.descricao: The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
issues.textoGolden: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

comentarios.texto: The newly added `s.search.TotalDocs()` call is unsafe: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs()` (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:144-150) iterates `b.cache` without holding `cacheMu`, while the bleve.go hunk in this same PR keeps `cacheMu` for the `b.cache[key] = idx` write only. Because search.go:207-213 already started the watch-event goroutine that can call `build` → `BuildIndex` → cache write, line 216 can iterate the map concurrently with that write, causing a `concurrent map iteration and map write` panic or data race. Either guard the `TotalDocs` read with `cacheMu`, or move this call to a point where no build can run concurrently.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs after launching the write-event listener, but bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates b.cache without cacheMu.RLock. A write event for an unindexed resource can concurrently publish an index through BuildIndex, causing a map iteration/write race and potentially a fatal runtime error during initialization. Protect TotalDocs cache iteration with the same read lock used by GetIndex.

BuildIndex now writes b.cache under Lock while TotalDocs (called from search.init after the watch goroutine starts) ranges over b.cache without any lock. This can cause a concurrent map read/write fatal error. Fix by taking cacheMu.RLock in TotalDocs.

issues.descricao: NewResourceServer returns an error when Init fails without cancelling the server context created earlier.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) and, on error, returns `nil, err` without invoking the `cancel` func created at line 229 and without running any lifecycle cleanup. WHY: Init may have already started long-lived goroutines — searchSupport.init's event-consumption loop uses context.Background() (resource/search.go:202) and initWatcher starts a watcher bound to s.ctx (server.go:752-770) — so if search.init succeeds and initWatcher (or a later step) fails, the constructor discards the server while those goroutines keep running with no way to stop them, leaking the internal context and watcher goroutines. HOW: on the error path call `cancel()` (and any needed lifecycle.Stop) before returning, or defer the cancel until success.

WHAT: NewResourceServer calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously but returns nil,err without calling the cancel created for s.ctx. WHY: Failed startup leaks the server context (and any lifecycle/watch resources partially started by Init), leaving goroutines/channel watches alive. HOW: On Init error call s.cancel() (and lifecycle Stop cleanup) before returning.
